articles.title: How brands’ deeper creator deals are unlocking cost efficiencies, results
articles.summary: Executives from Chili's, Disney and Alaska Airlines at Advertising Week New York described a shift from treating creators as add-ons to making them central to marketing strategy, with long-term partnerships now driving measurable business results. Chili's social media director Luz Bickert said a May campaign pairing pop star Lizzo's Baby Back Ribs jingle cover with creator Keila Pacheco's low-budget mukbang car video outperformed the brand's polished TV spot, and credited influencer partnerships with growing the Triple Dipper from 7% to 15% of total sales. Disney VP Nicole Leo said creator-led content now makes up over 40% of assets in media campaigns, up from under 10% five years ago, aided by a corporate restructuring that lets creator ideas flow between departments while still requiring customized briefs per project. Alaska Airlines' April Johnson noted that contracting creators long-term creates budget efficiencies and matches how talent prefers to work. Panelists agreed creators should be looped into campaign planning earlier rather than handed rigid briefs, and that combining influencer and media agency reporting helps prove the channel's value, even as brands still grapple with measuring engagement beyond paid impressions.
articles.li_summary: At Advertising Week New York, Chili's, Disney and Alaska Airlines executives revealed creators now drive 40%+ of Disney's media assets and helped grow Chili's Triple Dipper from 7% to 15% of sales through long-term, deeply integrated partnerships rather than one-off sponsored posts.

articles.title: TikTok broadens agentic AI play, brings global ad network to US
articles.summary: TikTok unveiled a broad set of advertising and commerce updates at Advertising Week New York, centered on AI-driven tools and U.S. expansion. The TikTok Ad Network (TTAN), previously used internationally, is now available to U.S. advertisers, letting them run campaigns across roughly 400,000 third-party apps through TikTok Ads Manager, with Integral Ad Science providing independent measurement for viewability, invalid traffic and brand safety. On the shopping side, TikTok introduced Buy Direct for in-feed purchases without leaving the app, a conversational Shopping Assistant that handles product, shipping and sizing questions, and an Agentic Leads tool for capturing high-intent prospects via DMs or website lead forms, supported by partners including Salesforce, Shopify, Shoplazza and Stripe. TikTok is also expanding Smart+ automation to search campaigns and launching Smart+ Creative Selection to streamline asset choices, alongside growing GMV Max for TikTok Shop merchants. A Model Context Protocol launched in May now connects to Claude, Kimi, Manus, Perplexity and Snowflake. TikTok says it helped generate $81 billion in U.S. GDP in 2025, with 54 million American shoppers buying after watching a TikTok video.
articles.li_summary: TikTok launched its U.S. TikTok Ad Network reaching 400,000 third-party apps, plus new AI tools including Buy Direct, a Shopping Assistant, Agentic Leads, and expanded Smart+ campaign automation, timed to Advertising Week New York.

articles.title: Meta adds parental oversight to Meta AI app
articles.summary: Meta has begun rolling out parental supervision tools for its dedicated Meta AI app, expanding oversight features first introduced in April for AI elements embedded across its other platforms. Once supervision is enabled, parents and guardians can review a seven-day log of topics their teen has raised with Meta AI, though actual conversation content remains private. Parents seeking tighter restrictions can switch from the default 13+ setting to a new Limited Content mode, which further narrows the kinds of exchanges teens can have with the chatbot. The move comes amid growing scrutiny of AI's role in teens' lives: Pew Research found 57% of U.S. teens have used chatbots for information searches and 54% for schoolwork help, while other reporting shows many are turning to AI for companionship and emotional support. The update may also lay groundwork for eventually opening Meta's Muse AI agents to younger users, aligning with the company's broader ambition to expand AI access widely. Still, while topic-level visibility gives parents a useful signal, it may not fully address deeper risks like misinformation, bias, or AI influence on adolescent decision-making.
articles.li_summary: Meta today launched parental supervision controls in its standalone Meta AI app, letting parents view the topics—but not full conversations—their teens discussed with the chatbot over the past seven days, plus a new Limited Content setting.

articles.title: Instagram tests option to open to Reels
articles.summary: Instagram is piloting a UI option, spotted by app researcher Radu Oncescu, that would let users choose to open directly into their Reels feed rather than the standard post feed when launching the app. Stories would still appear at the top of the home screen as usual, and users could swipe across to access the traditional feed, or revert back to the classic layout whenever they prefer, making this a toggleable setting rather than a forced redesign. Meta previously trialed a similar format in India last year, where the Stories bar sat above a Reels-first feed and a top-right icon let users jump to the traditional feed. The move reflects Reels' growing dominance: over 50% of time spent on Instagram now goes toward Reels, and the format is driving all of the platform's recent engagement growth. By framing this as an opt-in test rather than a default change, Meta can gauge adoption and avoid backlash, though wider Reels engagement gains could eventually push Instagram to make this the standard experience for all users.
articles.li_summary: Instagram is testing a new option letting users set Reels as their default home screen feed instead of the traditional post feed, with Stories still displayed on top and a one-tap switch back available anytime.

articles.title: TikTok outlines US election preparations
articles.summary: TikTok announced on Monday its preparation strategy for the November U.S. midterm elections, centered on four priorities: protecting user data and systems, detecting harmful or deceptive activity, promoting reliable election content, and securing accounts belonging to government officials and candidates. The company confirmed it continues working with Oracle to safeguard American user data, software, and app content, stating that every feature or code update undergoes security review before reaching U.S. users. For the election period specifically, TikTok is standing up a U.S. Election Mission Control Center to track emerging risks, coordinate investigations, and respond to threats in real time, alongside stepped-up monitoring for coordinated influence campaigns, AI-generated misinformation, and false claims. It also launched a new U.S. Election Center within the app to surface verified voting information. This marks the first major election test since TikTok's ownership shifted to a U.S.-based group, TikTok USDS, which was selected with input from President Trump and now oversees the platform's recommendation algorithm—raising scrutiny given Trump's past joking remark about making TikTok "100% MAGA."
articles.li_summary: TikTok detailed its U.S. midterm election safeguards on Monday, including a dedicated Election Mission Control Center, partnership with Oracle on data security, and a new Election Center for voting information, marking the first major vote since its U.S. ownership restructuring.

articles.title: Social media platforms resist U.K. safety disclosures
articles.summary: Ofcom, the U.K.'s digital regulator, is pushing forward sweeping Online Safety Act updates covering hate speech, CSAM, teen usage restrictions, livestreaming, and a May proposal requiring removal of non-consensual intimate imagery within 48 hours alongside new cyberflashing rules, with violations risking fines up to 10% of a company's global revenue. Meta, TikTok and X are now resisting, specifically objecting to February information notices demanding detailed content moderation metrics, including figures on removed or visibility-restricted posts and user exposure to harmful content. X called it the most burdensome regulatory request it has faced in any jurisdiction, while Meta argues Ofcom's demands exceed what's required under the EU's Digital Services Act, seeking more granular and wide-ranging data than European regulators require. This is notable since all three companies already comply with similar DSA disclosure rules in Europe. Ofcom maintains the expanded data is necessary to verify its regulatory approach is working, but the platforms see no clear justification for such broad requests. Ofcom aims to finalize most of these rules by year's end.
articles.li_summary: Meta, TikTok and X are challenging Ofcom's Online Safety Act proposals in the U.K., calling February's content moderation data requests unprecedented and more burdensome than even the EU's Digital Services Act disclosures.

articles.title: TikTok broadens agentic AI play, brings global ad network to US
articles.summary: TikTok unveiled a wave of advertising and commerce features timed to Advertising Week New York, headlined by the US debut of its TikTok Ad Network (TTAN), which lets brands run campaigns across roughly 400,000 third-party apps worldwide, integrated into TikTok Ads Manager with brand safety tools and independent measurement from Integral Ad Science. On commerce, TikTok introduced Buy Direct for in-feed purchases without leaving the app, a conversational Shopping Assistant for product, shipping and sizing questions, and an Agentic Leads tool to help marketers capture high-intent prospects via direct messages or website lead forms, backed by partners like Salesforce, Shopify, Shoplazza and Stripe. TikTok also expanded Smart+ automation to search ads and added Smart+ Creative Selection to streamline asset choices, while broadening GMV Max to factor in costs like affiliate commissions and coupons. The company cited a PF Global report crediting it with $81 billion in US GDP impact in 2025 and 54 million American shoppers influenced by its videos. Its Model Context Protocol, launched in May, now connects to AI platforms including Claude, Kimi, Manus, Perplexity and Snowflake.
articles.li_summary: TikTok launched its TikTok Ad Network in the US for the first time, giving advertisers access to about 400,000 third-party apps, alongside new AI shopping and lead-generation tools unveiled at Advertising Week New York.

articles.title: Influencer marketing has an AI trust problem
articles.summary: Meltwater and YouGov surveyed consumers on generative AI acceptance across content types and found influencer marketing ranks among the least accepted uses, with just 28% approval compared to 47% for product advertising and 53% for entertainment content. The report also found 86% of respondents want content to disclose AI use, and 59% said undisclosed AI would damage their trust in a brand. This contrasts with earlier virtual influencers like Lil Miquela and Shudu, whose artificiality was openly part of their appeal; today's AI-generated creators in testimonials and haul videos are often indistinguishable from real people, raising deception concerns. Instagram has responded by replacing its "AI Creator" label with a more direct "AI-generated profile" tag and restricting distribution for synthetic accounts that don't clearly disclose their nature, after finding users resent discovering a seemingly human profile is actually AI. The research and platform changes point to the same conclusion: brands running influencer programs need stronger vetting of creators, centralized monitoring of content published under their name, and consistent upfront disclosure whenever generative AI is involved, since concealment rather than AI use itself is what erodes consumer trust.
articles.li_summary: New Meltwater/YouGov research finds only 28% of consumers accept generative AI in influencer marketing versus 47% in advertising and 53% in entertainment, while Instagram now labels synthetic profiles "AI-generated" and limits their reach.

articles.title: X launches updated video composer
articles.summary: X has updated its video upload and posting interface, introducing a more streamlined composer layout centered on improved captioning tools, according to X developer Allegra Jacchia. Creators can now manually edit auto-generated captions directly in the composer or ask Grok, X's AI assistant, to correct errors automatically. Grok can also translate captions into other languages, making content more accessible to international audiences. This follows a string of video-focused updates from X this year: a major July overhaul added multi-language caption support and green screen recording, August brought new video overlay options, and most recently the platform expanded livestreaming capabilities to support better live broadcasts. The push reflects X's broader strategy of building native creation tools to encourage original content rather than reposted clips from other platforms, as the company competes for creator engagement. Video activity on X has been climbing steadily in recent years, though notably the company has quietly dropped the "video-first platform" branding it experimented with back in 2024.
articles.li_summary: X rolled out a redesigned video composer with a cleaner layout and editable captions that creators can manually fix or have Grok AI correct and translate into other languages.

articles.title: Instagram tests read-only mode
articles.summary: App researcher Alessandro Paluzzi has surfaced evidence that Instagram is developing a read-only mode for viewing profiles, likely as part of the paid Instagram Plus subscription add-ons. When activated, this mode would prevent users from liking or commenting on posts while browsing someone's profile, and would also block messaging, following, and viewing that person's Stories. The feature appears designed to let users browse profiles more freely without accidentally interacting with old content, such as liking a years-old post while scrolling through someone's history. While this could be useful for casual browsing, such as researching a potential date or new contact, it also raises concerns about enabling more covert surveillance of other users' accounts, since deep profile browsing often signals heightened interest beyond a casual visit. The feature hasn't been officially confirmed or launched by Instagram, and details on pricing or rollout timing remain unclear, but if added to the Plus package, it could make the subscription tier more appealing to users seeking additional privacy-oriented browsing tools.
articles.li_summary: Instagram is testing a read-only profile viewing mode, reportedly tied to its paid Instagram Plus add-on package, which blocks liking, commenting, messaging, following, or viewing Stories while browsing a profile.

articles.title: Instagram adds AI songs to DMs
articles.summary: Instagram has rolled out a new AI-powered song generation feature within its direct messaging inbox, first spotted by creator Jonah Manzano. Users now see an option to create a song directly in their DM sharing menu, which prompts them to enter custom lyrics and choose from various music genres before Instagram's AI generates a track to send to friends. Meta has described the addition as a fun way to boost engagement between users. The feature closely mirrors Snapchat's recently launched Snap-to-Song tool, which converts message text into song lyrics for paying subscribers, though Instagram's version gives users more freedom since there are no restrictions on what lyrics can be entered. While the tool could add a lighthearted, humorous element to private conversations, it stands in contrast to Meta's broader positioning of AI as a transformative, world-changing technology, raising questions about whether such novelty features align with or dilute that larger narrative about AI's serious potential.
articles.li_summary: Instagram has added an AI song creation tool to its DM inbox, letting users input custom lyrics and select a music genre to generate and send AI-made tracks to friends, similar to Snapchat's paid Snap-to-Song feature.

articles.title: Instagram adds Threads sharing sticker for Stories
articles.summary: Instagram has rolled out a new sticker for Stories that lets users repost Threads content directly into their Story frames. Spotted by creator Jonah Manzano, the sticker opens a selection menu showing Threads posts a user has previously liked or saved, as well as their own posts, allowing any of them to be overlaid onto a Story. This mirrors a recent Threads feature that let users quote-post content as image stickers, though that version only worked with shared images rather than full posts. The addition signals that cross-platform sharing between Instagram and Threads is still functional despite Meta's broader push to make Threads operate independently. Last month, Meta removed the requirement for advertisers to hold an Instagram account to run Threads campaigns, and it stopped using Instagram activity to shape users' Threads interest graphs. Even as Meta works to give Threads its own identity and audience, this new sticker shows the two apps remain technically linked, giving creators another avenue to extend the reach of their Threads posts.
articles.li_summary: Instagram launched a new Threads sharing sticker that lets users select any liked, saved, or self-authored Threads post and embed it directly into their Instagram Stories for added visibility.

articles.title: Sociable: TikTok adds certification tiers for agency partners
articles.summary: TikTok has restructured its Agency Partner Program, which launched in 2020 and now includes more than 600 approved agencies, into two distinct certification tiers. Agencies will now be designated as either an Agency Partner or a Premier Agency Partner, with the badge awarded reflecting an agency's proven performance, operational maturity, and certified staff expertise on the platform. The standard Agency Partner badge recognizes agencies that meet established benchmarks for platform competency and campaign execution, while the Premier Agency Partner badge is reserved for a smaller, select group of top-tier agencies worldwide that demonstrate consistent business results, advanced platform knowledge, and a strong focus on TikTok-first marketing strategies. TikTok says both tiers assure brands they are working with vetted specialists, whether the need is launching and scaling performance campaigns or executing large, complex brand activations requiring deeper expertise. The update is meant to give marketers clearer signals when selecting an agency partner, covering areas like creative production, marketing technology integration, and campaign measurement, ultimately helping brands match their specific needs with the right level of agency experience.
articles.li_summary: TikTok has split its 600+ agency Partner Program into two tiers, Agency Partner and Premier Agency Partner, to signal verified expertise and help brands choose vetted marketing partners.

articles.title: Reese’s searches for ‘trick-or-treatiest street’ in multichannel effort
articles.summary: Reese’s is running a multichannel Halloween campaign called “Reese’s Trick-or-Treatiest Street in America,” surveying 15,000 Americans and evaluating 150 candidate streets nationwide based on decorations, walkability and community participation, with results posted to a dedicated microsite. A newly formed Halloween Council, including “Addams Family” actor Christina Ricci, “Hocus Pocus” actor Kathy Najimy, and creators Rachel Iwanyszyn, Zaire Alford and Macy Blackwell, will review the data across a two-part social content series and crown one winning street on October 21. That street will receive a celebratory block party built with real estate partner Zillow, featuring Reese’s products and a fully decorated trick-or-treat setup, supported by a 60-second explainer video. The campaign also includes new creative tied to Reese’s ongoing “Everything Happens for a Reese’s” platform. The work comes from MiltonOne, Publicis Groupe’s dedicated Hershey unit, alongside Saatchi & Saatchi New York and MSL. The push follows the National Retail Federation’s projection of $13.5 billion in total Halloween spending this year, including $4.1 billion on candy, and arrives as Hershey reported 6.6% net sales growth to $2.7 billion in Q2 2026.
articles.li_summary: Reese’s launched “Trick-or-Treatiest Street in America,” surveying 15,000 people and 150 streets, with a celebrity-led Halloween Council naming a winner Oct. 21 for a Zillow-backed block party.

articles.title: Inside Advertising Week’s changes — and a bid for $100M in creator deals
articles.summary: Advertising Week New York kicks off Monday at Manhattan's Penn District through Oct. 8, continuing its shift from an agency-focused Madison Avenue event toward courting brand-side CMOs and marketing budget holders. Global president Ruth Mortimer says the creator economy is the area the conference has gone deepest into this year, with roughly 1,000 creators attending as delegates in 2025 expected to more than double in 2026. A new initiative, developed with chief creator officer Dhar Mann, aims to facilitate $100 million in creator-brand deals over the four-day event by matchmaking marketers' budgets with creators, building on a model that produced a real Old Navy campaign last year. Mortimer expects to surpass 2025's attendance of over 20,000 marketers. This marks the first Advertising Week since owner Emerald was acquired by Apollo Global Management and merged with Questex to form Forge. The event faces new competition the same week, including Lions' VidCon x Lions Creators showcase in Denver and the debut Jupiter Festival, backed by YouTube and the IAB, as the creator-marketing calendar grows increasingly crowded.
articles.li_summary: Advertising Week New York, running Oct. 6-8 at Penn District, is launching a challenge to generate $100 million in creator-brand deals while expecting creator attendance to more than double to over 2,000 in 2026.

articles.title: Concerns about social media’s negative impact are growing
articles.summary: Pew Research's latest global study across 37 nations shows that negative views of social media's impact on democracy have increased in every country surveyed since 2022. The U.S. stands out with 64% of adults saying social media harms democracy, while wealthier nations overall show higher skepticism than developing ones. Despite this, 55% of all respondents still see social media as net-positive for democracy, with younger adults most likely to hold favorable views. A separate Pew survey found 82% of Australian adults support restricting social media access for minors, with older respondents most supportive of such bans, mirroring the broader negative sentiment trend. Similar majority support for teen social media restrictions appears in the U.S., U.K., France, Italy, Norway, and Sweden. The findings suggest engagement-driven algorithms that amplify divisive, emotionally charged content may be fueling public concern, and point toward growing political momentum for age-based social media restrictions as public opinion increasingly favors limiting youth access to these platforms.
articles.li_summary: Pew Research's 37-nation survey found negative sentiment toward social media's impact on democracy has risen since 2022 in every country, with 64% of U.S. adults now calling it harmful.

articles.title: Meta’s Muse app surpasses 5M downloads and 3M weekly users
articles.summary: Meta's new Muse AI agent app has reached 5 million downloads within its first 22 days, according to Sensor Tower data cited by Yahoo Finance, placing it among just 23 apps in history to hit that milestone so quickly, and currently outperforming both ChatGPT and xAI's Grok in early adoption. The Information separately reported Muse has surpassed 3 million weekly active users, signaling strong retention alongside its rapid uptake. The app is central to Meta's consumer AI strategy, part of a broader commitment exceeding $600 billion in U.S. AI infrastructure spending over three years. At Meta's Connect conference, CEO Mark Zuckerberg detailed the monetization plan: Muse will remain free for users, with Meta eventually profiting from small fees on transactions the app facilitates, such as identifying and canceling unnecessary subscriptions. This targets a real pain point, since CNBC reports 44% of U.S. consumers increased subscription spending in 2025. Success depends on users granting Muse deeper access to personal and financial data, raising privacy concerns Meta hopes early cost-saving wins will help offset as adoption continues climbing.
articles.li_summary: Meta's Muse AI agent app has hit 5 million downloads in 22 days and surpassed 3 million weekly users, outpacing ChatGPT and Grok, with Zuckerberg planning to monetize via small fees on in-app transactions like subscription cancellations.

articles.title: TikTok US reports generating $81B in economic value
articles.summary: TikTok commissioned PF Global to produce a new U.S. economic impact report surveying 11,123 American adults and more than 5,000 businesses, over half of them SMBs, concluding that the platform generated upward of $81 billion in economic value, though that figure stems from estimated advertiser spend multiplied by industry revenue-to-GDP ratios rather than confirmed contribution data. The report found 69% of surveyed businesses consider TikTok essential, 83% say it helps attract customers, 93% reported sales increases from promoting on the platform, 80% said it helped them scale, and 75% have paid creators for promotional content. TikTok Shop reportedly averaged nearly 595,000 monthly live shopping sessions in the US during 2026, with live-driven sales up 92% year-over-year, while platform-driven discovery allegedly added $14 billion in spending across tourism, retail and hospitality. The report also claims TikTok enabled 3.6 billion hours of informal learning in 2025, with 45 million adults saying it clarified their career options. The timing suggests this is part of TikTok's ongoing effort to justify its U.S. presence, even though its American arm's sale to a local consortium already appears to secure its future in the country.
articles.li_summary: TikTok released a PF Global-conducted report claiming the platform generated $81 billion in U.S. economic value, based on survey responses from 11,123 adults and over 5,000 businesses, though the GDP figure relies on estimated ad spend rather than verified data.

A newly formed Halloween Council, including "Addams Family" actress Christina Ricci, "Hocus Pocus" star Kathy Najimy and creators Rachel Iwanyszyn, Zaire Alford and Macy Blackwell, will review the data through a two-part social content series before naming the winning street on October 21. The chosen street will host a block party in partnership with Zillow, featuring Reese's products and a themed trick-or-treat experience, supported by a 60-second explainer video. The campaign also includes new creative built on Reese's existing "Everything Happens for a Reese's" platform, developed by Publicis-owned MiltonOne alongside Saatchi & Saatchi New York and MSL. The push comes as Hershey, Reese's parent company, reported $2.7 billion in second-quarter 2026 net sales, up 6.6%, and 8.7% growth for the first half of the year, as Halloween spending nationally is projected to reach $13.5 billion, including $4.1 billion on candy.

articles.summary: Advertising Week New York kicked off Monday at Manhattan's Penn District, continuing its multi-year shift from agency-focused programming toward courting brand-side CMOs who control budgets, according to global president Ruth Mortimer. A major new push targets the creator economy: working with chief creator officer Dhar Mann, the event introduced a four-day challenge aiming to generate $100 million in creator-brand partnerships by actively matching marketers' budgets with creators, building on a 2025 Old Navy collaboration that started as an Advertising Week concept. Creator attendance, roughly 1,000 delegates last year, is projected to more than double in 2026. Overall attendance is expected to top 2025's 20,000-plus marketers. This is the first Advertising Week since owner Emerald was acquired by Apollo Global Management in July and merged with Questex to form Forge, a deal that's also opening doors to healthcare-related content and sister brands like StreamTV Show. IAB data shows U.S. creator economy ad spend is projected to grow nearly 19% to $44 billion in 2026.
articles.li_summary: Advertising Week New York, running Oct. 6-8 at the Penn District, is launching a challenge to broker $100 million in creator-brand deals while expanding creator attendance from 1,000 to an expected 2,000+ in 2026.

articles.title: Reddit ends support for RSS feeds
articles.summary: Reddit announced two developer tool changes aimed at protecting its data from automated scraping and bots. First, RSS feed support will end on November 13, 2026, since Reddit says RSS has become a major vector for large-scale scraping; moderators who rely on RSS for alerts are urged to migrate to Devvit apps before the deadline, though no alternative exists for non-moderator RSS use. Second, Reddit is folding its public data API into its Developer Platform, eliminating the previously available free, limited API access for approved developers and making all data access paid. These moves continue a years-long effort to monetize and restrict outside access to Reddit's data, following 2023 API price hikes, a 2024 Public Content Policy update, and lawsuits against scrapers allegedly supplying data to OpenAI and Meta. In Q2, Reddit's non-advertising revenue, largely driven by data licensing, hit $42 million, up 24% year-over-year. The changes also come as a PromptWatch report found Reddit citations in ChatGPT responses fell sharply last month, underscoring pressure to protect and formalize its AI data licensing deals.
articles.li_summary: Reddit will discontinue RSS feed support on November 13, 2026 to curb data scraping, and is shifting its public API entirely to paid-only access via its Developer Platform.

articles.title: Instagram adds option to boost livestreams
articles.summary: Instagram has introduced a new in-app feature allowing creators to boost their live videos as ads, joining existing options to promote posts, Stories and Reels. Under this update, a live broadcast itself becomes the ad creative, with the promoted content eligible to appear across Feed, Stories and Instagram Reels to expand audience reach. Creators can activate the boost either right before going live or schedule it in advance, with Instagram recommending at least a two-hour lead time to avoid ad delivery delays. The promotion only runs while the creator is actively broadcasting, aiming to funnel active users into the live audience in real time. While advertisers could previously set up similar promotions through Meta Ads Manager, this update simplifies the process by letting creators launch a boost straight from the livestream composer, selecting a target audience (or using Instagram's suggested option) and setting start and end times, without needing to build a full ad campaign manually.
articles.li_summary: Instagram now lets creators boost live videos as ads directly from the in-app livestream composer, with promotions running only while broadcasting and appearing in Feed, Stories and Reels.

articles.title: TikTok hosts launch of David Geffen Galleries
articles.summary: TikTok expanded its Museums Alive initiative by partnering with the Los Angeles County Museum of Art to livestream the debut of its David Geffen Galleries directly within the app. The broadcast featured LACMA curators walking viewers through the museum's Egyptian collection alongside live musical performances, giving TikTok's largely younger user base a front-row view of the new space without visiting in person. This builds on TikTok's growing track record of cultural programming, having previously run similar livestream collaborations with New York's Metropolitan Museum of Art and MoMA, as well as the Grand Egyptian Museum in Giza. The platform's first Museums Come Alive event took place in May, bringing together a broader lineup of cultural institutions, and TikTok says these events have collectively drawn millions of viewers. The strategy reflects TikTok's positioning as a hub for music and cultural trends, and signals an effort to use that influence to connect younger audiences with art, history, and museum experiences they might otherwise overlook in favor of purely digital entertainment.
articles.li_summary: TikTok partnered with LACMA this week to livestream the launch of its new David Geffen Galleries, featuring curator-led tours of the Egyptian collection and live music as part of its Museums Alive series.

articles.title: LinkedIn updates its AI-powered hiring bot
articles.summary: LinkedIn rolled out Hiring Assistant 2, the next version of its AI-powered recruiting tool, now live in the app with stronger reasoning, memory and personalization features designed to surface better candidate matches. Rather than simply finding someone who fits a job title, the bot can now factor in patterns like location preference, industry background and experience level based on a recruiter's past hiring history. The update also adds more transparency into why candidates are matched, plus signals on how likely someone is to respond, drawing on platform activity, Open to Work status and InMail engagement. LinkedIn is layering in trust indicators such as verifications to flag legitimate candidates, expanding connected-app listings so users can showcase outside skills, adding new candidate-management integrations, and introducing voice capability for pre-screening calls. The company says more than 20,000 businesses already use its agentic hiring tools, with recruiters four times more likely to contact candidates sourced through Hiring Assistant than via traditional recruiting, and response likelihood up 27% compared to six months ago, a figure these latest upgrades aim to push even higher.
articles.li_summary: LinkedIn launched Hiring Assistant 2, an upgraded AI recruitment bot with improved reasoning, memory and personalization, now used by over 20,000 companies to source candidates four times more likely to be contacted than through traditional methods.

articles.title: TikTok adds certification tiers for agency partners
articles.summary: TikTok has revamped its Agency Partner program, introducing a two-tier badge system to help brands identify agency expertise levels. Partners now receive either an Agency Partner badge or a Premier Agency Partner badge. The standard Agency Partner badge marks agencies that show strong performance, operational capability, and certified team knowledge of TikTok's ad tools. The Premier Agency Partner badge is reserved for a smaller, select group of top-performing agencies worldwide, representing the highest recognition tier, awarded based on proven business results, deep platform knowledge, and consistent focus on TikTok-first marketing strategies. Both badges are meant to give brands confidence that an agency has passed TikTok's vetting requirements, whether they need help launching standard performance campaigns or executing large-scale, specialized activations. The updated system is intended to make it easier for marketers to choose the right partner for their needs. TikTok's Agency Partner program launched in 2020 and now includes more than 600 approved partners spanning creative production, marketing technology, and measurement services.
articles.li_summary: TikTok restructured its Agency Partner program, splitting its 600+ approved marketing partners into two new certification tiers, Agency Partner and Premier Agency Partner, to signal expertise levels to brands.

articles.title: Instagram updates its educational safety program
articles.summary: Instagram announced updates to its School Partnerships program, which launched in March 2025 and now includes almost 17,000 participating schools. The program lets educators report safety concerns directly to Instagram through a prioritized channel for approved contributors with direct student contact. New features include in-app hubs for school accounts to widen message reach, plus access to channels, School Stories, and Notes for participating schools, alongside added resources for educators, parents, and students. Instagram is also introducing "verified students," giving approved student contributors similar alert and connection tools to flag concerns, along with new student banners and directories that let classmates find each other—visible only to mutual teen followers at the same school. Meta has partnered with Unidays to verify high schoolers before granting access to official school communities, aiming to keep these spaces secure. The rollout comes as Instagram faces ongoing scrutiny and regional usage restrictions over concerns about social media's impact on teen mental health and wellbeing.
articles.li_summary: Instagram expanded its School Partnerships program to nearly 17,000 schools, adding in-app school hubs, verified student accounts, student directories, and Unidays-based verification to strengthen teen safety reporting and connections.

articles.title: Meta adds contributor badges to Forums chat app
articles.summary: Meta rolled out new features for its Forums app, launched in May to turn Facebook Groups into a Reddit- or Quora-style Q&A platform, including recognition badges for top contributors, a display of related answers pulled from multiple groups, and topic labels to improve content discovery. The badges reward users who consistently answer questions, share firsthand experience, offer practical advice, or spark community discussions, and come with perks like faster-publishing posts, intended to motivate experts to keep contributing. A new cross-group answer feature lets users compare responses to similar questions from different communities and pick the most helpful one. Topic labels are meant to make it easier for people to find relevant discussions. While Meta frames these updates as improvements for everyday users, the underlying goal appears to be generating structured, high-quality question-and-answer data, similar to how Reddit content has become valuable for training and guiding AI chatbot responses, suggesting Forums may ultimately serve Meta's AI systems more than its human community members.
articles.li_summary: Meta added top-contributor badges, cross-group related answers, and topic labels to its Forums Q&A app, aiming to boost expert engagement and feed higher-quality data into its AI chatbot responses.

articles.title: Pinterest offers post-holiday marketing tips
articles.summary: Pinterest this week published new marketing tips focused on Q5, the week between Christmas and New Year's, which it describes as a high-engagement period despite falling outside typical holiday campaign windows. The platform outlined three shifts marketers should make: first, pivot creative from gift-giving scenarios to personal, everyday use cases; second, move messaging away from festive celebration toward planning, organization and self-improvement themes that align with new-year mindsets; and third, replace holiday urgency around shipping deadlines with messaging that emphasizes how products support daily routines and long-term goals. Pinterest noted that campaign focus should vary by objective—awareness campaigns should lean into fresh-start inspiration, consideration campaigns should show how products fit evolving routines, and sales-focused campaigns should use product-led creative to drive quick action. To help brands execute this shift without building entirely new assets, Pinterest pointed to its ad tools, Media Library and Smart Assembly feature, which repurposes existing creative into new ad formats tailored to the post-holiday mindset shift from gifting toward self-care and personal use.
articles.li_summary: Pinterest released post-holiday marketing guidance this week, urging brands to shift Q5 (Dec 26-31) campaigns from gift-focused messaging toward self-purchase, planning and routine-based content to match changing consumer intent.

articles.title: Meta launches Muse AI for SMBs
articles.summary: Meta expanded its agentic AI push by launching Muse for Small Business, building on its earlier consumer-focused Muse agents to give small business owners dedicated automation tools. The core feature is Muse connectors, integrations with partner apps including Zoom, Figma, Canva, Stripe, GitHub, QuickBooks, Slack and Shopify, alongside Meta's own tools and analytics, letting Muse access business data to run background tasks automatically. Meta Chief AI Officer Alexandr Wang said plumbers, grocery store owners and farmers are already using Muse to find efficiencies. Example use cases include analyzing content to build promotional campaigns, reviewing cash flow to flag savings opportunities, drafting customer communication responses, and refining marketing and business plans; Meta is also developing goal-setting features to align Muse activity with specific business targets. Meta says users retain control, with nothing published, sent or spent without explicit approval, though the system's usefulness depends heavily on how much data access SMBs are willing to grant. A lower-risk starting point could be using Muse simply for Facebook and Instagram strategy tips before granting deeper operational access.
articles.li_summary: Meta launched Muse for Small Business, an agentic AI package with connectors to Zoom, Figma, Canva, Stripe, GitHub, QuickBooks, Slack and Shopify to help SMBs automate marketing, finances and customer communication workflows.

articles.title: Threads expands live chat engagement options
articles.summary: Threads announced updates to its live chat feature on Tuesday, expanding on the tool it launched in April 2025 for text-based group discussions hosted within the app's DM section. The update introduces Live Reactions, letting participants send a shared emoji that floats across every viewer's screen simultaneously, rather than reacting to individual messages. A new raise-hand feature lets users signal they want to join an active chat, useful for sessions where the host has capped participant numbers. Threads is also bringing live chats to the web for the first time, responding to one of its most-requested feature requests, and is extending access to users in Australia as part of its ongoing rollout. The company highlighted past chat activity tied to Coachella, KATSEYE, the NBA, World Cup and Jay-Z as evidence of engagement, and is now partnering with creators for live chats around "Dancing with the Stars" and the WNBA Playoffs. Threads head Connor Hayes said in a Tuesday post that the feature's goal is to keep the app feeling timely and help users find relevant real-time conversations.
articles.li_summary: Threads rolled out live chat upgrades on Tuesday, adding group emoji reactions, a raise-hand feature for joining discussions, web-based access, and expanded availability to users in Australia.
